# 2 Samuel Chapter 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 175v–176r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_008_page_001.jpg, 2SA_008_page_002.jpg

---

**1** After this David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and David took Metheg-ammah from the hand of the Philistines.

**2** He defeated Moab and measured them with a line, making them lie down on the ground. He measured two lines to be put to death and one full line to be kept alive. And Moab became servants to David, bringing tribute.

**3** David defeated Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to restore his power at the River Euphrates. **4** David captured from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. David hamstrung all the chariot horses but left enough for a hundred chariots.

**5** When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of the Arameans. **6** David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became servants to David, bringing tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

**7** David took the shields of gold that were carried by the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem. **8** From Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a very great amount of bronze.

**9** When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer, **10** Toi sent his son Joram to King David to greet him with blessings, because David had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him — for Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. Joram brought with him articles of silver, gold, and bronze.

**11** These also King David dedicated to the LORD, together with the silver and gold that he dedicated from all the nations he subdued — **12** from Aram, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, Amalek, and from the plunder of Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

**13** David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down the Edomites in the Valley of Salt — eighteen thousand men. **14** He put garrisons throughout all of Edom, and all the Edomites became David's servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.

**15** David reigned over all Israel, and David administered justice and righteousness to all his people.

**16** Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder; **17** Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was secretary; **18** Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David's sons were priests.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 1 — Metheg-ammah:** The phrase is left as a transliterated proper noun, as its meaning is uncertain. It may refer to the "bridle of the chief city" (i.e., political control of Gath). The parallel in 1 Chronicles 18:1 clarifies: "David took Gath and its surrounding towns."

**Verse 2 — Measuring with lines:** The grim precision of the measuring-line execution is preserved without commentary. This was David's treatment of defeated Moab — a two-thirds execution rate.

**Verse 13 — "Edomites" (emendation):** The MT reads "Aram," but the Valley of Salt context and the 1 Chronicles 18:12 parallel confirm "Edom." The resh/daleth confusion is well-attested in Hebrew manuscripts. I emend silently to "Edomites."

**Verse 18 — "priests":** The MT says David's sons were *kohanim* (priests). This likely means "chief officials" or "royal advisors" — a secular use of the priestly title. The Chronicler's parallel (1 Chr 18:17) reinterprets as "chief officials."

*— LOGOS*
